summary: Windows Hello fingerprint DB SID collision after image restore prevents new enrollments
description:
Issue summary:
After depot image restores (repair returns) some Windows devices fail to enroll fingerprints via Windows Hello. Enrollment UI returns an immediate failure and event logs show WinBio/DPAPI errors that indicate keyset/container issues. This started appearing after we circulated a set of captured images used for rapid rebuilds that were not fully generalized.

Impact:
- Affected users cannot enroll fingerprints after repair or image restore; blocking local passwordless login and causing higher helpdesk volume for MFA/password resets.
- Occurs intermittently across multiple device families; appears correlated with restores using non-generalized captures.

Environment:
- Prod fleet (image capture + SCCM/OSD re-deploy pipeline)
- Windows 11 22H2 and newer builds used in our imaging catalog
- Devices observed: Dell Latitude 7440, HP EliteBook 860 G9 (but likely broader)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Capture a device image without running sysprep/generalize (lab image used for depot restores).
2) Restore that image to a different physical device via SCCM OSD.
3) Boot, complete autopilot/MDM join and BitLocker reprovisioning flow as per standard depot return.
4) Attempt to enroll fingerprint via Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options > Windows Hello Fingerprint.
5) Enrollment fails immediately with UI error: "Something went wrong. Try again later."

Observed logs/artifacts:
- Windows Event Viewer: Microsoft-Windows-WinBio/Operational shows Event ID 21 and 22 with error text referencing DPAPI/NGC container not accessible.
- System/Application logs show Win32 error codes: 0x80090016 (NTE_BAD_KEYSET) and occasional 0x8009002F.
- Ngc folder ACLs look correct for LocalSystem/ServiceProfiles but SID references appear to point to original machine SID embedded in the captured image.
- No BitLocker recovery required in observed cases, but clearing TPM was attempted in two incidents and required manual BitLocker key escrow and re-provisioning.

Expected behavior:
- Enrollments should succeed after image restore once device completes device-join and TPM provisioning.

Hypothesis / preliminary root cause:
- Images captured without sysprep/generalize retain original machine SIDs and Ngc/WinBio container bindings. When restored to a different hardware instance, Windows Hello/WinBio expects DPAPI/NGC containers keyed to the new machine/TPM. Because the image still references the old SID/container, enrollment attempts hit DPAPI keyset errors.
- The issue surface is amplified when images are used across models that have different TPM provisioning flows.

Temporary workaround tried:
- Manual deletion of the local Ngc profile (C:\Windows\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Ngc) followed by reboot and reinitialization allowed enrollment on one device, but on another device removing the folder required clearing the TPM and re-provisioning BitLocker (high risk).
- Creating a new local admin account and attempting enrollment under that profile did not consistently succeed.

Suggested next steps / mitigation plan:
1) Immediate: Stop using the latest non-generalized image for depot restores. Revert to the previous image that was captured with sysprep/generalize until we have a permanent fix.
2) Imaging process: Audit capture pipeline to enforce sysprep/generalize before image cataloging; add a CI check that validates machine SID is randomized.
3) Recovery tooling: Build a safe, documented remediation script that can be run by depot technicians to reset NGC/WinBio bindings without clearing TPM or forcing BitLocker recovery. Script to be validated on test devices first.
4) Long term: Move to Autopilot/OOBE-based provisioning for repaired units where feasible so machine identity is provisioned consistently.

Attachments (screenshots/log snippets) available in ticket attachments area and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/internal/INT-221678/
comments: 2026-03-11 - Sasha Patel: Filed after two depot returns reported by L1. Both users returned devices after SSD replacement; both devices were imaged with the recently promoted build. Assigned to imaging squad for triage.
2026-03-11 - Jonah Kim: Looking into logs; initial suspicion is leftover container/SID mapping in Ngc. Can we get a copy of the exact image used for the two devices and the capture notes?

2026-03-12 - Priya Rao (Imaging): Confirmed the failing image was captured without sysprep/generalize as part of a rushed capture. We have halted further depot use of that image.
Reference capture job: SCCM-CAP-2026-02-28-rapid

2026-03-12 - Jonah Kim: Reproduced issue in lab by deploying same image to a fresh Dell 7440. Event logs match reporter. Deleting Ngc folder allowed enroll on lab device after reboot (no TPM clear) — suggest scripted safe removal and test across models. Will coordinate with security before wide use.

2026-03-13 - Security/Compliance (Amir Hassan): Clearing TPM is a risky operation given BitLocker; any remediation must include BitLocker key escrow flow. Do not perform TPM clear on production devices without PM approval.
2026-03-13 - Jonah Kim: Agreed. Updating ticket with temporary mitigation: revert image in pipeline and add validation gate. Working on a non-destructive remediation script and test plan.
investigation_notes: Verified reproduction on Dell 7440 with captured image. WinBio service logs point to DPAPI keyset errors referencing original machine SID. Ngc ACLs contain S-1-5-21-... values matching capture source. No full disk encryption data loss observed in lab when only Ngc folder removed, but behavior is inconsistent across models. Need additional test matrix (Dell/HP/Lenovo) to confirm safety of scripted deletion. Escalated to imaging lead and security for clearance on remediation steps.
resolution_plan: 1) Roll back to previous generalized image in SCCM catalog (complete). 2) Add CI check and enforce sysprep/generalize for future captures (in progress). 3) Develop remediation script: safe Ngc cleanup + service restart + enrollment validation; test across 10 devices per model family before deployment (planned). 4) Documentation update: Add runbook for depot technicians describing steps and AV/backup verification. Owner: Imaging team (Priya Rao). Target: complete by 2026-03-20.
notes_for_followup:
- Confirm whether any users experienced BitLocker escrow after attempted TPM clear and document recovery tickets.
- Add telemetry to detect future NGC/WinBio enrollment failures (WinBio event id thresholds) and alert imaging team.
- Communicate to depot techs via #support-depot Slack channel to stop using the bad capture immediately.
